applicationWindow: High school students interested in completing a university research experience for credit are instructed to contact the principal investigator directly by email. Undergraduate students interested in research or volunteering may also inquire. Participation depends on current laboratory availability and applicable university requirements.
ratingNote: An unusually explicit direct-access research opportunity because the laboratory specifically tells high school students seeking a university research experience for credit to contact the PI. Students can gain experience designing experiments, collecting and analyzing scientific data, and communicating research findings.
summary: The D'Orazio Laboratory at the University of Kentucky conducts research in microbiology, immunology, molecular genetics, and infectious disease. High school students seeking a university research experience for credit are explicitly invited to contact the principal investigator. Laboratory trainees learn how to design and conduct controlled experiments, analyze results, and communicate scientific research.

name: JSeeliger Lab
title: Molecular Biology and Microbiology Summer Research Placement
applicationWindow: High school students interested in a full-time summer placement should contact Dr. Jessica Seeliger and submit a cover letter and CV. The laboratory instructs prospective high school researchers to submit their materials by December preceding the desired summer placement.
ratingNote: An excellent individual-lab opportunity with unusually clear instructions for high school applicants. Students can apply directly to the PI for a full-time summer research placement by submitting a cover letter and CV, providing a genuine pathway into university molecular biology and microbiology research.
summary: The JSeeliger Lab at Stony Brook University conducts research at the intersection of molecular biology, microbiology, biochemistry, bacterial biology, and pharmacology. High school students can apply for full-time summer research placements by sending Dr. Jessica Seeliger a cover letter and CV by the preceding December, making this an unusually direct route into an individual university research laboratory.

name: High School Research Internship
title: Economics Research Department Internship
applicationWindow: The 2026 High School Research Internship posting has closed. The position was offered through the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis Research Department. Students should monitor future Minneapolis Fed career postings to determine whether another high school research internship cycle becomes available.
ratingNote: An exceptional economics opportunity because the high school intern works within a Federal Reserve research department and receives supervision and mentorship from a research economist. The position provides exposure to professional economic research, technical skills, and the work of economists within the Federal Reserve System.
summary: The Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis has offered a High School Research Internship within its Research Department for students interested in economics. The selected intern works with a research economist serving as a supervisor and mentor while developing economics research and technical skills. The 2026 posting has closed, so students should monitor the Minneapolis Fed for future cycles.

name: National High School Fed Challenge
title: Applied Economics Research and Publication Challenge
applicationWindow: The National High School Fed Challenge is open to eligible students in grades 9 through 12. The research theme and submission schedule can change each year, so students should review the Federal Reserve Board's official program page for the current theme, registration information, and deadlines.
ratingNote: A strong nationwide economics research opportunity because students conduct original research, analyze evidence, and produce an academic-style submission around an annual economics theme. Outstanding submissions may be selected by Federal Reserve staff for publication in the Journal of Future Economists.
summary: The National High School Fed Challenge is a Federal Reserve economics research competition for students in grades 9 through 12. Participants investigate an annual economics theme, conduct research, analyze economic evidence and data, and produce an academic submission. Outstanding student work may be selected for publication in the Federal Reserve's Journal of Future Economists.

name: Polk Presidential Scholars
title: Faculty-Mentored Public Policy and Political Economy Research Fellowship
applicationWindow: Students interested in the Polk Presidential Scholars program should review the Blackwell Research Institute's official program page for current eligibility requirements, fellowship dates, application deadlines, and availability.
ratingNote: A strong social-science and economic-policy research opportunity because students work with university faculty to develop, conduct, and present original policy research. It is especially relevant for students interested in economics through political economy, governance, institutions, and public policy.
summary: The Polk Presidential Scholars program provides high school students with faculty-mentored experience conducting original policy research. Scholars develop research questions, investigate issues involving policy, governance, institutions, and public life, and present their findings. The fellowship is particularly relevant to students interested in economic policy, political economy, and interdisciplinary social-science research.

name: Economics Policy Academy
title: Economic Policy Research Program
department: Summer Programs for High School Students
applicationWindow: The 2026 Economics Policy Academy residential and commuter sessions are full. Students interested in future sessions should review Georgetown University's official summer program page for updated application dates, eligibility requirements, tuition, and availability.
ratingNote: A useful economics and policy research experience where students investigate economic-policy questions and develop a research-based poster. Topics span development economics, inequality, behavioral economics, international trade, fiscal and monetary policy, and foreign aid, although the academy is more structured than a traditional research assistant position.
summary: Georgetown University's Economics Policy Academy introduces high school students to economic analysis and public policy. Students investigate topics including development economics, behavioral economics, inequality, international trade, fiscal and monetary policy, and foreign aid. Participants apply their learning to economic-policy questions and develop a research-based poster.

name: Hematian Research Group
title: Direct Chemistry Research Opportunity
university: University of North Carolina at Greensboro
applicationWindow: High school, community college, and undergraduate students interested in joining the Hematian Research Group may inquire directly. High school students are encouraged to email the lab with information about their future goals, chemistry background, and reasons for wanting to join the research team. Participation depends on current research and mentor availability.
ratingNote: An excellent direct-access chemistry opportunity because the lab explicitly provides research opportunities beginning at the high school level and gives students clear instructions for contacting the research group. Students can gain exposure to active inorganic chemistry, electrochemistry, and biochemistry research.
summary: The Hematian Research Group at UNC Greensboro conducts research involving inorganic chemistry, electrochemistry, biochemistry, and related chemical processes. The group explicitly provides research opportunities for students beginning at the high school level. Interested high school students are instructed to email the lab directly describing their chemistry background, future goals, and interest in joining the research team.

name: Tong Lab
title: Analytical and Environmental Chemistry Volunteer Research Internship
applicationWindow: High school students interested in possible volunteer research internships are instructed to contact Dr. Tong directly. Applicants may be asked to submit a personal statement, CV, and two recommendation letters, with an on-site interview for students under consideration. Opportunities depend on current laboratory availability.
ratingNote: A particularly strong individual-lab opportunity because Georgetown explicitly provides high school students with a direct route to apply for volunteer research internships. The application process is substantial and can lead to hands-on experience in analytical and environmental chemistry research.
summary: The Tong Lab at Georgetown University conducts analytical and environmental chemistry research involving chemical measurement and laboratory instrumentation. High school students interested in volunteer research internships may contact Dr. Tong directly. Applicants can be asked to provide a personal statement, CV, and recommendation letters and may complete an interview before being accepted into the lab.

name: Smith Research Group
title: High School Chemistry Summer Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Motivated high school students interested in summer chemistry research are encouraged to contact Professor Smith directly. Prospective students should email the research group and explain their interest in science and chemistry in approximately four to five paragraphs. Availability depends on current summer research capacity.
ratingNote: A rare and highly direct chemistry research opportunity because the group explicitly recruits motivated high school students for summer research and provides detailed instructions for contacting the professor. Students can gain experience in spectroscopy, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, and laboratory research.
summary: The Smith Research Group at Iowa State University and Ames Laboratory offers summer research opportunities for motivated high school students interested in science and chemistry. Prospective students are instructed to contact Professor Smith directly and describe their research interests and motivation. The group's research includes spectroscopy, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, and related chemical measurement techniques.

name: J. L. Holmes Mass Spectrometry Facility
title: Analytical Chemistry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: Research projects and student opportunities may become available periodically at the J. L. Holmes Mass Spectrometry Facility. The facility has hosted high school students as well as university researchers. Interested students should review the facility's current research and contact information to inquire about available opportunities.
ratingNote: A highly specialized analytical chemistry opportunity offering exposure to professional research instrumentation including mass spectrometry and chromatographic methods. High school students have previously participated in the facility, although opportunities depend heavily on current research needs and supervision availability.
summary: The J. L. Holmes Mass Spectrometry Facility at the University of Ottawa supports research involving analytical chemistry, mass spectrometry, gas chromatography, liquid chromatography, and chemical analysis. The facility has hosted high school students and other student researchers, and research or volunteer opportunities may become available depending on current projects and laboratory capacity.

name: High School Chemistry Research
title: Faculty-Connected Chemistry Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: University of Cincinnati Chemistry notes that high school students have connected with faculty members and continued research projects within the department. Opportunities are not guaranteed and depend on individual faculty interest and laboratory availability. Eligible students may also explore ACS Project SEED placements associated with the department.
ratingNote: A useful faculty-connection pathway because the Chemistry Department documents previous high school students working with university faculty and continuing their research projects at Cincinnati. Unlike a formal internship, placement depends on identifying a faculty mentor willing and able to support the student's work.
summary: The University of Cincinnati Department of Chemistry has supported high school students who connect with faculty members and continue research projects within university laboratories. Students interested in chemistry research may explore faculty mentorship opportunities, although placements depend on individual faculty and laboratory availability. The department also participates in ACS Project SEED opportunities for eligible students.

name: Needleman Lab
title: Biophysics and Quantitative Biology Research Opportunity
department: School of Engineering and Applied Sciences
applicationWindow: The Needleman Lab explicitly welcomes inquiries from students interested in potential research projects. High school students have contributed to past and current projects. Interested students may contact current lab members and/or Professor Daniel Needleman to discuss possible projects, with participation dependent on research needs and available mentorship.
ratingNote: An exceptional direct-access Harvard research opportunity because the lab explicitly documents high school participation and invites interested students to discuss possible projects. High school researchers can work with graduate students or postdoctoral mentors on independent questions involving quantitative biology, microscopy, image analysis, and biophysical experimentation.
summary: The Needleman Lab at Harvard University conducts quantitative and experimental research at the intersection of biology, physics, and engineering. High school students have contributed to past and current projects and may work with graduate students or postdoctoral researchers on independent research questions. Interested students are encouraged to contact lab members and/or Professor Daniel Needleman to discuss potential projects.

name: Shafiee Laboratory
title: Biomedical Engineering High School Research Opportunity
university: Harvard Medical School / Brigham and Women's Hospital
applicationWindow: The Shafiee Laboratory maintains recruitment information for prospective researchers, including a dedicated high school intern category. Interested students should review the laboratory's current positions page and follow its application instructions. Availability depends on current projects and mentorship capacity.
ratingNote: A rare Harvard-affiliated individual-lab opportunity with explicit recruitment information for high school interns. Students can gain exposure to cutting-edge biomedical engineering research involving diagnostics, biosensing, microfluidics, nanotechnology, biomaterials, and microfabrication.
summary: The Shafiee Laboratory at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital develops biomedical technologies involving microfluidics, biosensing, nanotechnology, biomaterials, diagnostics, and microfabrication. The laboratory's recruitment page explicitly includes high school interns and provides a direct pathway for interested students to seek research involvement.

name: Visual Attention Lab — Jeremy Wolfe
title: Visual Cognition and Neuroscience Research Opportunity
university: Harvard Medical School / Brigham and Women's Hospital
applicationWindow: High school participation in the Visual Attention Lab is available through Harvard Medical School's Project Success pathway rather than unrestricted direct laboratory applications. Students should review Project Success for current eligibility requirements, application dates, and program availability.
ratingNote: An outstanding psychology and neuroscience research opportunity with a long documented history of mentoring high school students. Professor Jeremy Wolfe has hosted Project Success researchers for more than two decades, and previous high school participants have made meaningful contributions to peer-reviewed laboratory research.
summary: The Visual Attention Lab led by Professor Jeremy Wolfe studies visual attention, perception, cognition, and related areas of psychological and neuroscience research. The lab has hosted high school researchers through Harvard Medical School's Project Success program for more than two decades. High school participants work within an active research environment and can make substantive contributions to ongoing projects.

name: RWE Laboratory
title: Medical AI Research and Scientific Observership Opportunity
university: Massachusetts General Hospital / Harvard Medical School
applicationWindow: The RWE Laboratory primarily advertises research internships for undergraduate students. In exceptional cases, highly talented high school students in grades 11 or 12 may be considered individually for a scientific observership. Interested students should review the laboratory's current positions page and submit the requested application materials if eligible.
ratingNote: A highly selective Harvard-affiliated medical AI opportunity. High school participation is not the standard pathway, but the laboratory explicitly states that exceptional juniors and seniors may be considered individually. This makes it a legitimate but reach-level option for students with unusually strong backgrounds in AI, programming, data science, or biomedical research.
summary: The RWE Laboratory at Massachusetts General Hospital conducts research involving medical artificial intelligence, healthcare data, biomedical informatics, and real-world clinical evidence. Research internships are primarily designed for undergraduate students, but the laboratory states that exceptional high school juniors and seniors may occasionally be considered for scientific observership opportunities on an individual basis.

name: Science Research Mentoring Program
title: Year-Long Astrophysics Research Mentorship
applicationWindow: The Science Research Mentoring Program serves eligible students from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School. Participants conduct year-long independent astrophysics research with scientists at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian. Students should verify current eligibility and application information for future cycles.
ratingNote: An exceptional year-long astrophysics research opportunity where eligible high school students work directly with professional scientists on independent projects. Geographic and school eligibility are extremely narrow, but the depth of mentorship and sustained research involvement make it highly valuable for qualifying students.
summary: The Science Research Mentoring Program at the Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian pairs eligible Cambridge Rindge and Latin School students with scientists for year-long independent astrophysics research. Participants develop and conduct substantial research projects under professional scientific mentorship, gaining long-term exposure to astronomy and astrophysical research.

name: Chandra Lab
title: Neuroscience and Parkinson's Disease Research Placement
applicationWindow: The Chandra Lab is participating in Yale Pathways Research Internships for 2026. Eligibility is limited to qualifying public high school students from the New Haven area. Students should review Yale Pathways for current application cycles and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional hands-on neuroscience placement where high school students contribute to active Yale research involving Parkinson's disease and cellular pathology. The 2026 project includes techniques such as cryosectioning, immunohistochemistry, microscopy, image analysis, and basic R, with no prior research skills required.
summary: The Chandra Lab at Yale School of Medicine studies neurological disease and cellular mechanisms related to disorders such as Parkinson's disease. Through Yale Pathways, high school students can participate in active laboratory research. The 2026 project examines Parkinson's-related pathology in the spinal cord and introduces students to cryosectioning, immunohistochemistry, microscopy, image analysis, and basic R.

name: Saxena Lab
title: Computational Neuroscience and AI Research Placement
applicationWindow: The Saxena Lab is participating in Yale Pathways Research Internships for 2026. Participation is available to qualifying public high school students from the New Haven area through the Yale Pathways application process.
ratingNote: An outstanding interdisciplinary research opportunity combining neuroscience, artificial intelligence, machine learning, and computational modeling. The 2026 high school project involves creating a virtual marmoset model using real movement recordings to investigate neural control of behavior.
summary: The Saxena Lab at Yale uses computational modeling and machine learning to study how neural activity produces movement and behavior. Through Yale Pathways, high school students can contribute to active research projects. The 2026 project involves building a virtual marmoset model from experimental movement data to explore sensorimotor processing and brain dynamics, with Python experience considered helpful.

name: Massilani Lab
title: Ancient DNA and Human Evolution Research Placement
applicationWindow: The Massilani Lab is listed as a participating laboratory in the 2026 Yale Pathways Research Internship program. Eligible New Haven-area public high school students should apply through Yale Pathways and verify future lab participation each cycle.
ratingNote: A highly distinctive genetics research opportunity exposing high school students to ancient DNA, genomics, population genetics, and human evolution. The unusual research focus makes this especially valuable for students interested in genetics, anthropology, evolutionary biology, or computational genomics.
summary: The Massilani Lab at Yale conducts research involving ancient DNA, genetics, genomics, and human evolution. Through Yale Pathways, high school students can be placed into the laboratory to gain exposure to active genetic and evolutionary research involving ancient biological material and questions about human population history.

name: O'Hern Lab
title: Mechanical Engineering and Materials Research Placement
applicationWindow: The O'Hern Lab is participating in the 2026 Yale Pathways Research Internship program. Eligible New Haven-area public high school students apply through Yale Pathways, with laboratory placements determined by the program and participating research groups.
ratingNote: A strong engineering research placement that gives high school students exposure to active work in mechanical engineering, materials science, and computational simulation. Projects involving material properties and molecular-dynamics methods provide a valuable alternative to the biomedical-heavy research opportunities common at the high school level.
summary: The O'Hern Lab at Yale conducts research in mechanical engineering and materials science, including the study of material properties and molecular-dynamics simulations. Through Yale Pathways, high school students can gain exposure to computational and physical approaches used to understand materials and engineering systems.

name: Natarajan Lab
title: Astrophysics and Black Hole Research Placement
applicationWindow: The Natarajan Lab is listed as a participating research group for the 2026 Yale Pathways Research Internship program. Eligible New Haven-area public high school students should apply through Yale Pathways and verify the lab's participation in future cycles.
ratingNote: An exceptional astrophysics opportunity where eligible high school students can gain exposure to research on black holes, galaxies, and cosmic structure within an active Yale astronomy group. The specialized focus makes this one of the strongest astronomy listings in the database.
summary: The Natarajan Lab at Yale University conducts astrophysics research focused on black holes, galaxy formation, and the evolution of cosmic structure. Through Yale Pathways, eligible high school students can be placed into the lab and gain exposure to active theoretical and computational astronomy research.

name: SCALE Lab
title: Mechanical Engineering and Imaging Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The SCALE Lab has hosted high school researchers and directs prospective members to contact the laboratory about joining. Participation depends on current projects, available mentorship, and laboratory capacity.
ratingNote: A rare direct-access Cornell engineering opportunity with documented high school participation. Current high school research in the lab has involved micro-CT imaging, Python-based image processing, 3D reconstruction, and experimental analysis, making this especially valuable for students interested in engineering, computation, and materials research.
summary: The SCALE Lab at Cornell Engineering conducts interdisciplinary research involving mechanical engineering, mechatronics, imaging, materials, and computational analysis. The lab currently documents high school research participation, including work involving micro-CT imaging, Python image processing, 3D reconstruction, and compression experiments. Prospective students can contact the laboratory to ask about possible research involvement.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology — Faculty and Mentor Research Volunteering
title: Ecology and Ornithology Research Volunteer Opportunity
applicationWindow: High school students age 16 or older may explore volunteer opportunities at the Cornell Lab of Ornithology. Prospective researchers are encouraged to identify faculty members or mentors whose projects match their interests and inquire about volunteering or research involvement. Individual opportunities and age requirements vary by project.
ratingNote: A highly valuable direct-inquiry pathway because Cornell explicitly encourages prospective students to identify relevant researchers and inquire about project involvement. The Lab of Ornithology offers access to internationally recognized work in ecology, conservation, wildlife biology, ornithology, and biological data science.
summary: The Cornell Lab of Ornithology provides pathways for students to become involved in research and volunteering related to birds, ecology, conservation, and biological data. High school students age 16 or older may participate in eligible volunteer activities. Students interested in research are encouraged to explore faculty and mentor projects and inquire directly about opportunities that align with their interests.

name: Boyce Thompson Institute High School Research Experience
title: Plant Science and Computational Biology Research Experience
applicationWindow: The program is designed for eligible local and regional high school students age 16 or older. Students should review the Boyce Thompson Institute's official program page for current application deadlines, eligibility requirements, stipend information, and future summer cycles.
ratingNote: An excellent hands-on research experience where students work on real projects with both a graduate or postdoctoral research mentor and a faculty mentor. Participants gain experience in areas such as plant molecular biology, bioinformatics, biological engineering, and plant-biotic interactions and present their work at a research symposium.
summary: The Boyce Thompson Institute High School Research Experience gives students six weeks of mentored research in plant science and related biological fields. Participants work on active projects with graduate or postdoctoral mentors and faculty researchers, attend laboratory meetings, read scientific literature, prepare a research proposal, and present their work at a final research symposium.

name: VTPMD 2990 Research in Epidemiology
title: Veterinary Epidemiology Research Apprenticeship
university: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine
applicationWindow: Qualified unmatriculated high school students may participate through Cornell Summer College when eligible. Cornell undergraduates may also enroll. Students should verify current course availability, prerequisites, and Summer College access before planning around this opportunity.
ratingNote: An unusually niche Cornell research pathway that can place qualified high school students into active epidemiology research under graduate students, postdoctoral researchers, or faculty. Participants complete a defined research project, deliver an oral presentation, and prepare a manuscript in publication-style format.
summary: VTPMD 2990 is a mentored epidemiology research apprenticeship through Cornell's College of Veterinary Medicine. Qualified high school students participating through Cornell Summer College may work in research laboratories under graduate researchers, postdocs, or faculty. Students complete a designed epidemiology project, analyze their findings, present their work orally, and prepare a manuscript in a format suitable for scientific publication.

name: High School Catalyst Program
title: Biomedical Laboratory Research Program
applicationWindow: Participation requires eligibility through the NYBioForce pathway. Students should review Weill Cornell Medicine's official High School Catalyst Program page for current prerequisites, application requirements, program dates, and future participation information.
ratingNote: A substantial biomedical research placement where high school students spend approximately 25 hours per week working in an active laboratory under a graduate student, staff scientist, or postdoctoral mentor. The NYBioForce prerequisite makes access more restricted, but the depth of hands-on research is excellent for eligible students.
summary: The Weill Cornell Medicine High School Catalyst Program provides eligible high school students with six weeks of intensive laboratory research. Participants are paired with graduate students, staff scientists, or postdoctoral researchers to develop and conduct an in-person research project. Students gain experience planning and performing experiments and present their work at both a closing event and a public research symposium.

name: Youth Leadership Advisory Board (YLAB)
title: Youth Social Media Research Collaboration
applicationWindow: The Youth Leadership Advisory Board operates through the Cornell Social Media Lab and involves motivated high school students in research about issues young people face online. Students should review the lab's current YLAB information for participation details, future cohorts, and application availability.
ratingNote: A highly distinctive social-science opportunity because high school students help shape academic research rather than simply observing it. Participants contribute youth perspectives to research questions involving social media, online behavior, communication, and digital wellbeing.
summary: The Youth Leadership Advisory Board at Cornell's Social Media Lab connects academic researchers with motivated high school students to study issues affecting teenagers online. Students participate in the research process and help researchers better understand youth experiences involving social media, communication, digital wellbeing, and online behavior.

name: CURTA-Y
title: Urban Sustainability Participatory Research Program
department: Just Places Lab — College of Architecture, Art, and Planning
applicationWindow: CURTA-Y has involved high school students from the Binghamton and Vestal areas in Cornell-led participatory research through 2026. Students should review the Just Places Lab's current project information for future cohorts, local eligibility, and participation opportunities.
ratingNote: A strong and unusual social-science research opportunity because high school students participate as co-researchers alongside Cornell students. Projects use real qualitative, quantitative, and community-based methods to investigate sustainability, urban development, circularity, and public policy.
summary: CURTA-Y is a participatory research initiative through Cornell's Just Places Lab that involves high school students as co-researchers in studies of sustainable development and community change. Participants have used interviews, photography and video, community mapping, building-carbon estimates, and policy research to investigate circularity and sustainability in local communities.

name: Cornell Hydroponics Learning Labs
title: Paid Urban Agriculture and Sustainability Internship
department: Cornell University Cooperative Extension — New York City
applicationWindow: The Hydroponics Learning Labs operate through participating New York City public schools. Eligible students at participating campuses may be selected for paid internships. Availability depends on school participation and the current Cornell Cooperative Extension program cycle.
ratingNote: A highly niche paid opportunity combining sustainability, agriculture, environmental science, and hands-on technical work. Students work directly with hydroponic systems, crop production, and water quality, and some participants develop independent projects addressing community food-system issues.
summary: Cornell Cooperative Extension's Hydroponics Learning Labs operate within participating New York City public-school campuses. Paid high school interns spend time working with hydroponic systems, water quality, crop production, transplanting, and harvesting. Some students also develop independent projects using survey data or other research methods to investigate food access and sustainability.

name: CNF ATLAS
title: Nanofabrication and Cleanroom Research Facility Experience
department: Cornell NanoScale Science and Technology Facility
applicationWindow: The ATLAS experience launched in 2026 for local high school seniors participating through the TST-BOCES New Visions Engineering program. Students should verify future availability through Cornell's NanoScale Science and Technology Facility and the relevant partner-school program.
ratingNote: An unusually advanced engineering experience because high school students gain hands-on access to Cornell's professional nanofabrication cleanroom and learn techniques used in micro- and nanotechnology research. Eligibility is very geographically restricted, and the experience is more facility-based than an independent research assistant placement.
summary: CNF ATLAS is a Cornell NanoScale Science and Technology Facility experience that gives eligible local high school seniors hands-on exposure to nanotechnology and microfabrication. Students receive safety and technical training and work inside Cornell's 17,000-square-foot cleanroom, gaining experience with tools and processes used in semiconductor, materials, and nanoscale engineering research.

name: Lovette Lab
title: Ornithology and Evolutionary Biology Research Connection
department: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology / Cornell Lab of Ornithology
applicationWindow: Professor Irby Lovette explicitly invites high school students with serious interests in his research areas to email him with their background, interests, and current year in school. The lab generally cannot place minors directly into its molecular genetics facility, but Professor Lovette may provide guidance, connect students with appropriate Cornell opportunities, or help arrange research-related meetings when feasible.
ratingNote: A valuable professor-level connection opportunity because the PI explicitly invites serious high school students to contact him. This should not be treated as a guaranteed laboratory internship, since minors generally cannot work directly in the lab's molecular genetics facility, but students may receive guidance or connections to appropriate Cornell research opportunities.
summary: The Lovette Lab at Cornell studies ornithology, evolutionary biology, avian genomics, and related ecological questions. Professor Irby Lovette explicitly invites serious high school students interested in these areas to email him with their background and interests. Although the laboratory generally cannot host minors directly in its molecular genetics facility, he may help connect students with appropriate Cornell or Lab of Ornithology opportunities and research contacts.

name: Bugaj Lab
title: Bioengineering and Synthetic Biology Research Placement
applicationWindow: High school research participation in the Bugaj Lab is supported through Penn's Office of Outreach, Education & Research pathway. Penn has identified a research project led by Professor Christopher Bugaj that supports a summer high school researcher. Students should review Penn OER for current eligibility, application dates, and future placement availability.
ratingNote: An exceptional faculty-level Penn research opportunity with documented support for a high school researcher. The underlying project involves engineering thermal biosensors for remote control of mammalian cells, providing exposure to synthetic biology, bioengineering, cellular engineering, and experimental biomedical research.
summary: The Bugaj Lab at the University of Pennsylvania conducts bioengineering and synthetic biology research involving the development of technologies for controlling and studying cellular behavior. Penn's Office of Outreach, Education & Research has identified a project led by Professor Christopher Bugaj that supports a summer high school researcher working on thermal biosensors for remote control of mammalian cells.

name: Penn Center for Musculoskeletal Disorders — Soslowsky Research
title: Musculoskeletal and Orthopedic Research Placement
applicationWindow: The Penn Center for Musculoskeletal Disorders supports high school summer researchers through Penn's Office of Outreach, Education & Research Summer Internship Program. Students should review Penn OER for current Philadelphia-area eligibility requirements, deadlines, and future summer application cycles.
ratingNote: A strong biomedical research opportunity with explicit infrastructure for high school participation. Penn reports that the Center's Learning on a Limb initiative supports multiple summer high school researchers through OER, giving students access to active research in musculoskeletal biology, orthopedics, biomechanics, and related biomedical fields.
summary: The Penn Center for Musculoskeletal Disorders conducts interdisciplinary research involving orthopedics, musculoskeletal biology, biomechanics, and biomedical engineering. Through its Learning on a Limb initiative and Penn OER, the Center hosts high school researchers during the summer and connects them with active Penn research environments.

name: Penn OER Summer Research Internship
title: Paid Biomedical Faculty-Lab Research Internship
department: Perelman School of Medicine — Office of Outreach, Education & Research
applicationWindow: The Penn OER Summer Research Internship serves eligible Philadelphia-area high school students. Participants receive preparatory research training followed by placement in Penn faculty laboratories. Students should verify current eligibility requirements, deadlines, dates, and application availability through Penn OER for each summer cycle.
ratingNote: An outstanding paid biomedical research opportunity where high school students receive actual research positions hosted by Penn faculty. Participants receive preparation in laboratory skills, scientific literature, experimental methods, and research documentation before conducting hands-on bench research with mentorship from Penn trainees and laboratory staff.
summary: The Penn OER Summer Research Internship provides eligible high school students with paid biomedical research experience at the Perelman School of Medicine. Students complete preparatory training and then spend six weeks in research positions hosted by Penn faculty, where they work with laboratory trainees and staff while contributing to hands-on basic biomedical research.

name: Penn Research Experience for High School Students (PREHSS)
title: Faculty-Mentored Multidisciplinary Research Experience
applicationWindow: PREHSS places participating high school students with research laboratories and mentors at the University of Pennsylvania. Students should review the official program page for current eligibility requirements, available disciplines, application dates, and future summer cycles.
ratingNote: A particularly valuable multidisciplinary opportunity because students are assigned to an active Penn research laboratory and mentor rather than simply taking a pre-college course. Research areas can include biology, chemistry, physics, astronomy, linguistics, psychology, and other disciplines, and students present their research at the conclusion of the experience.
summary: The Penn Research Experience for High School Students places participants into University of Pennsylvania research laboratories where they work with mentors on current scientific research. Projects may span biology, chemistry, physics, astronomy, linguistics, psychology, and related disciplines. Students gain direct research experience and present their work at the end of the program.

name: GRASP High School Internship
title: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Research Internship
applicationWindow: High school students interested in research within Penn's robotics and artificial intelligence ecosystem are directed toward the GRASP high school internship pathway. Students should review GRASP's current information for application availability, eligibility requirements, deadlines, and participating research projects.
ratingNote: An exceptional engineering research pathway into one of Penn's major robotics and autonomous-systems research communities. Penn research groups explicitly direct interested high school students toward the GRASP high school internship rather than unsolicited individual-lab applications, providing a documented route into robotics and AI research.
summary: The GRASP High School Internship provides a pathway for high school students interested in robotics, artificial intelligence, computer vision, autonomous systems, and related engineering research at the University of Pennsylvania. Penn research groups such as the Lifelong Machine Learning group direct high school students toward this dedicated internship pathway for potential research involvement.

name: HIP-SAT
title: Paid MIT Research Laboratory Internship
applicationWindow: HIP-SAT is designed for eligible homeschooled high school students who can commute to MIT or arrange local housing. The 2026 program provides an eight-week summer research placement. Students should review the official HIP-SAT site for future application dates, eligibility requirements, compensation, and participating laboratories.
ratingNote: An exceptional MIT research opportunity because students are placed directly into active research laboratories and mentored by MIT PhD students or postdoctoral researchers. Participants contribute to frontier research, attend project meetings, develop scientific communication skills, and present their work at a final symposium.
summary: MIT's Homeschool Internship Program for Science and Technology places eligible high school students into active MIT research laboratories for an eight-week summer experience. Students work under PhD student or postdoctoral mentorship on projects that may involve laboratory experiments, scientific programming, theory, data processing, literature research, and scientific communication. The 2026 program is paid.

name: MIT PRIMES
title: Year-Long Mathematics and Computational Research Program
applicationWindow: MIT PRIMES serves eligible high school sophomores and juniors in the Greater Boston area. The 2026 cycle is underway, and applications for the 2027 cycle are expected to become available in September 2026. Students should verify current eligibility requirements and deadlines on the official MIT PRIMES site.
ratingNote: One of MIT's strongest high school research opportunities because students work on genuine unsolved problems under academic mentorship rather than completing predetermined classroom projects. Research areas include mathematics, computer science, bioinformatics, and computational biology.
summary: MIT PRIMES is a year-long research program for highly motivated Greater Boston high school students. Participants work with academic mentors, often MIT graduate students or postdoctoral researchers, on unsolved research problems in mathematics, computer science, bioinformatics, and computational biology.

title: Remote Year-Long Mathematics and Computer Science Research Program

summary: PRIMES-USA is MIT's remote research program for high school students living outside the Greater Boston area. name: LEAH Knox Scholars Program

name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
title: Independent STEM Research Mentorship and Funding Program

summary: The MIT THINK Scholars Program supports high school students who have developed promising STEM research ideas but need mentorship or resources to carry them out. name: Pediatrics Internship Program at Stanford (PIPS)
title: Pediatrics Faculty-Lab Research Internship

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)

summary: The Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program is an eight-week research experience for high school students interested in biomedical science and medicine. Participants work on active Stanford research projects with faculty, postdocs, students, and researchers in areas including immunology, cancer biology, neuroscience, stem cell and regenerative medicine, bioinformatics, and cardiovascular research.

name: FAST Summer Research Internship
title: Paid Stanford Laboratory Research Internship
department: Future Advancers of Science and Technology (FAST)
applicationWindow: The FAST Summer Research Internship is available to eligible current FAST students who are at least 16 years old and are not graduating seniors. summary: The FAST Summer Research Internship provides selected current FAST students with paid research placements in Stanford laboratories. Interns spend eight weeks working approximately six hours per day on research projects with Stanford mentors. Projects can span biology, psychology, computer science, engineering, and other STEM disciplines.

name: RAMP UP / STaRS
title: Dental Regenerative Medicine Research Internship
applicationWindow: RAMP UP provides research opportunities for eligible high school and community college students through Stanford Medicine's STaRS research infrastructure. ratingNote: A highly specialized Stanford biomedical research opportunity focused on dental regenerative medicine. name: Personality Across Development Lab (PADLab)
title: Developmental Psychology Research Internship

summary: Northwestern's Personality Across Development Lab studies personality, development, behavior, and mental health across the lifespan. The lab explicitly accepts a small class of high school interns each summer. Interested students can apply directly by submitting a resume and short statement explaining their interest and fit with the laboratory.

name: Northwestern University Research Program for High Schoolers (NURPH)
title: Paid Materials Science and Engineering Research Program
applicationWindow: NURPH serves eligible rising high school juniors and seniors from the Chicago and Evanston areas. ratingNote: One of Northwestern's strongest high school research opportunities. summary: The Northwestern University Research Program for High Schoolers places eligible local students into active Materials Science and Engineering research projects. Participants work on faculty-sponsored research with graduate-student mentorship in areas such as nanomaterials, sustainability, polymers, manufacturing, biomaterials, and energy-related materials. name: SciHigh

summary: SciHigh is a Northwestern NUGoKidney program that connects high school students with scientists and research laboratories for mentored biomedical research. name: Continuing Umbrella of Research Experience (CURE)

applicationWindow: CURE accepts eligible graduating high school seniors and early college students from qualifying underserved populations. summary: Northwestern's Continuing Umbrella of Research Experience provides eligible graduating high school seniors and early college students with training and research exposure in cancer science. name: Pathology & Laboratory Medicine Summer Research Internship
title: Biomedical Pathology Research Internship

ratingNote: A strong Brown medical research opportunity because students are individually assigned to active research laboratories and work on specific scientific projects with researchers. name: Ocean, Climate & Ecosystems (OCE) Data Science Research Internship

ratingNote: An exceptional environmental research opportunity because students receive long-term mentorship and develop personalized research projects rather than completing a short canned exercise. name: DEEPS CORES Research Internship

summary: Brown's DEEPS CORES initiative provides eligible Providence-area high school students with paid research internships in Earth, environmental, ocean, climate, and planetary science. name: RI ACS Project SEED — Brown Chemistry

name: PCTA Robotics Internship

applicationWindow: The internship is available through Brown's partnership with Providence Career and Technical Academy and is designed for eligible pre-engineering students. Students should verify current participation requirements through PCTA and Brown Computer Science.

name: Biophysics: Experiment & Computational Modeling

summary: This Princeton Physics research placement gives eligible high school students experience in experimental and computational biophysics. Depending on the project, students can gain experience with Python, MATLAB, machine learning, microscopy, imaging, microfluidics, soft robotics, and other research techniques before producing a final poster.

name: Modeling Disease Dysregulation Using Large Genomic Datasets

ratingNote: A standout computational biology opportunity because students work with large genomic datasets and apply statistical and machine-learning approaches to genuine biological questions. The project is unusually accessible because Princeton states that previous research and programming experience are not required.
summary: This Lewis-Sigler Institute research project introduces high school students to computational genomics and disease biology. Students work with a mentor to analyze large genomic datasets and develop or apply statistical and machine-learning approaches to questions involving cell types, genetic variation, genome function, development, aging, and disease.

name: Study & Engineering of New Enzymes for Biocatalytic Peptide Synthesis

ratingNote: An exceptional hands-on chemistry and biochemistry placement involving techniques used in active molecular research. Student contributions can include quantum and optical design, computational work, data analysis, literature research, and software development.

High school researchers assist with data collection and preprocessing for computational linguistic analysis and text classification. The broader research environment uses behavioral experiments, functional neuroimaging, machine learning, and other methods to study the self and social cognition.

name: BRAINYAC

Students conduct mentored brain research and present their work through a final scientific poster.

name: Science Matters Research Internship (SMRI)

Students assist faculty and researchers on real projects and accumulate approximately 150 hours of laboratory experience.

summary: The Detroit Research Internship Summer Experience connects eligible Cass Technical High School students with University of Michigan Chemistry laboratories. Students can gain practical experience with techniques and concepts including DNA extraction, gel electrophoresis, genetics, biomaterials, biotechnology, and scientific imaging.
summary: Rice Bio Academies provide high school students with hands-on university laboratory experiences through BioTech, BioMed, and BioEng programs. Depending on the academy, students explore biotechnology, biomedical science, bioengineering, genetics, biomaterials, DNA analysis, laboratory techniques, and scientific imaging.

name: seed2STEM
title: Paid Multidisciplinary Research Internship
applicationWindow: seed2STEM serves eligible Indigenous high school students in Grades 9 through 12 through Metro Vancouver and Kelowna-area pathways. The 2026 program runs from July 6 through August 14 for approximately 20 hours per week. Students should review the official program information for future application dates, regional eligibility, and participating research sites.
ratingNote: An exceptional Canadian high school research opportunity because students are placed into active research groups across dozens of departments and affiliated research sites. Host researchers develop genuine six-week projects that can involve laboratory work, data analysis, literature research, knowledge translation, and other forms of STEM research.
summary: seed2STEM provides eligible Indigenous high school students with paid six-week research internships across UBC Vancouver, UBC Okanagan, affiliated health-research sites, and other participating institutions. Students work with research mentors on real projects in fields including biomedical science, psychology, biology, engineering, and other STEM disciplines before presenting their work at a research showcase.

name: Peter D. Paré Scholarship
title: Heart and Lung Research Summer Internship
applicationWindow: The Peter D. Paré Scholarship is available to eligible high school students age 16 or older in Grades 11 or 12 who first complete the Centre for Heart Lung Innovation's High School Student Science Week. Selected students may then participate in an eight-week summer research internship. Students should verify current application dates and scholarship availability with HLI.
ratingNote: A strong biomedical research pathway because students can progress from hands-on laboratory exposure into an extended eight-week research internship at a major heart and lung research centre. The program provides sustained mentorship and experience with professional biomedical research.
summary: The Peter D. Paré Scholarship at UBC's Centre for Heart Lung Innovation gives eligible high school students the opportunity to continue from the centre's Science Week into an eight-week summer research internship. Participants gain experience in cardiovascular, respiratory, biomedical, and laboratory-medicine research while working within an active academic research environment.

name: Biomedical Engineering Research Trainee
title: Faculty-Lab Biomedical Engineering Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: McGill Biomedical Engineering notes that local high school students may exceptionally be accepted as research trainees. Prospective students are instructed to contact individual faculty members directly to inquire about potential research opportunities. Participation depends on faculty interest, project availability, eligibility, and departmental approval.
ratingNote: An unusually valuable Canadian professor-level pathway because McGill explicitly acknowledges that high school students can sometimes participate as research trainees and directly tells prospective students to contact individual faculty members about laboratory opportunities.
summary: McGill University's Department of Biomedical Engineering provides a research-trainee pathway through which local high school students may exceptionally join faculty laboratories. Interested students can identify faculty whose research matches their interests and contact them directly about opportunities in biomedical engineering, bioengineering, medical technology, biomaterials, and related research areas.

name: Andrade Lab High School Research
title: Animal Behavior and Ecology High School Lab Placement
applicationWindow: The Andrade Lab has previously hosted Grade 11 and 12 high school students through local school co-op placements. Students have assisted with laboratory research and, in some cases, undertaken more independent responsibilities. Current availability is not guaranteed, so interested students should verify whether the co-op pathway is active before pursuing a placement.
ratingNote: A strong individual-lab pathway with documented high school participation in animal-behavior and ecology research. Some motivated high school students have progressed beyond basic laboratory assistance into greater responsibility or independent research, though current availability should be confirmed.
summary: Professor Maydianne Andrade's laboratory at the University of Toronto Scarborough studies animal behavior, evolution, ecology, and arachnology, including research involving black widow spiders. The lab has hosted Grade 11 and 12 high school co-op students who assist with laboratory work, and some experienced students have taken on more advanced or independent research responsibilities.

name: GeoX
title: Earth and Environmental Science Field Research Experience
applicationWindow: GeoX is designed for high school students entering Grades 11 and 12. The 2026 program runs from August 9 through August 15 and combines field and laboratory activities. Students should review the University of Waterloo's current program page for future dates, fees, application deadlines, and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: A useful hands-on Earth and environmental science experience, although it is more research exposure than an independent research placement. Students gain experience with field mapping, environmental sampling, laboratory testing, geological interpretation, and professional scientific instruments.
summary: GeoX at the University of Waterloo gives high school students a one-week immersive experience in Earth and environmental science. Participants conduct field mapping and sampling, test soil and water, study geological structures and fossils, visit university research laboratories, and use professional tools related to geochemistry, hydrology, geophysics, and environmental research.

name: Student Advancement Research (StAR) Program
title: Paid Biomedical Laboratory Research Program
applicationWindow: The StAR Program serves eligible Grade 11 and 12 students who are at least 16 years old and meet the program's current eligibility requirements. Participants are matched with SickKids research laboratories for six weeks. The 2026 program runs from July 6 through August 14. Students should review the official SickKids information for future application dates and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional biomedical research opportunity because high school students are paired with active SickKids research laboratories, work directly with research staff, complete their own research projects, and present their findings at a research symposium.
summary: The Student Advancement Research Program at SickKids gives eligible high school students a six-week research experience inside one of Canada's leading pediatric research institutions. Participants are matched with research laboratories, work with research staff on individual projects, and gain experience in fields that can include genetics, cancer, neuroscience, pediatrics, and biomedical science before presenting their findings.

name: WISEST Summer Research Program
title: Paid University STEM Research Placement
department: Women in Scholarship, Engineering, Science and Technology
applicationWindow: The WISEST Summer Research Program is designed for eligible students who have completed Grade 11 and are entering Grade 12. Participants spend six weeks working as student researchers in University of Alberta research environments. The 2026 program runs from July 2 through August 13. Students should review current WISEST information for future application deadlines and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: A substantial university research experience because high school students spend six weeks working as student researchers within University of Alberta research environments. Placements can span engineering, biology, chemistry, computing, physics, and other STEM disciplines.
summary: The University of Alberta's WISEST Summer Research Program places eligible Grade 11 students into university research environments for six weeks. Participants work as student researchers while gaining hands-on experience in disciplines such as engineering, biology, chemistry, computing, physics, and other STEM fields.

name: High School Youth Researcher Summer (HYRS)
title: Paid Health Research Summer Program
department: Alberta Innovates / University of Calgary Research
applicationWindow: HYRS serves eligible Grade 11 students from Central Alberta who meet the program's current academic and regional requirements. Participants complete six weeks of full-time research under University of Calgary faculty mentorship. Placements may involve wet-laboratory or computational and dry-lab research. Students should review the current program information for application dates and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: A strong faculty-mentored research experience because high school students contribute to active biomedical and health research for six weeks. Placements can include experimental laboratory research or computational and data-focused projects, and students present their work at a final research symposium.
summary: The University of Calgary's High School Youth Researcher Summer program gives eligible Grade 11 students six weeks of faculty-mentored health research experience. Participants contribute to biomedical or health-related projects in wet-lab or computational research settings and conclude the program by presenting their research at a symposium.

name: Young Engineers and Scientists (YES!) Fellowship
title: Particle Physics and Engineering Research Fellowship
applicationWindow: The YES! Fellowship is designed for eligible graduating British Columbia secondary-school students who will enter post-secondary education. Fellows spend approximately six weeks at TRIUMF experiencing an active research-laboratory environment. Students should review the current fellowship page for application deadlines, award amounts, travel support, housing support, and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional physics and engineering opportunity because students spend six weeks inside TRIUMF, Canada's particle accelerator centre, gaining experience in a professional scientific research environment. The fellowship is particularly valuable for students interested in particle physics, nuclear physics, accelerator science, engineering, materials science, or scientific computing.
summary: TRIUMF's Young Engineers and Scientists Fellowship gives graduating British Columbia secondary students an immersive six-week experience at Canada's particle accelerator centre. Fellows gain exposure to professional research in particle and nuclear physics, engineering, accelerator science, materials science, scientific computing, and related fields while working within a major national laboratory.

name: Summer Psychology Research Initiative (SPRINT)
title: High School Psychology Research Program
applicationWindow: SPRINT is a free summer research initiative for eligible high school students studying in Ontario. The program introduces students to psychology while providing experience with psychological research and the university research environment. Students should review the University of Toronto Department of Psychology's current information for future dates and application requirements.
ratingNote: A valuable psychology-specific research opportunity because it allows Ontario high school students to gain research experience within the University of Toronto's psychology community. It also broadens research access beyond the biomedical and engineering opportunities that dominate many high school research databases.
summary: The University of Toronto's Summer Psychology Research Initiative gives Ontario high school students an opportunity to explore psychology while gaining experience with psychological research. Participants are introduced to behavioral and experimental psychology, cognitive science, research methods, and the broader academic research environment.

name: Vanderbilt Basic Sciences — Faculty-Sponsored High School Research Internships
title: Faculty-Sponsored Biomedical Research Internship Pathway
applicationWindow: This is not a centralized high school application program. Vanderbilt Basic Sciences allows high school students to conduct research in faculty laboratories when a willing Vanderbilt faculty member agrees to sponsor the student. Participation depends on faculty interest, laboratory capacity, project suitability, university approval, and completion of required intern procedures.
ratingNote: An exceptional hidden research pathway because Vanderbilt explicitly maintains an administrative mechanism for faculty-sponsored high school research interns. Students who secure a willing PI may conduct genuine educational research inside an active Basic Sciences laboratory rather than participating only in outreach or shadowing.
summary: Vanderbilt School of Medicine Basic Sciences allows high school students to conduct research in faculty laboratories through a faculty-sponsorship pathway. Students must identify a suitable Vanderbilt research group and secure a willing faculty sponsor, after which the university can process the student as a research intern. Potential fields include molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, neuroscience, and other biomedical sciences.

name: Zhou Lab
title: Structural and Cellular Biology Research Internship Pathway
applicationWindow: The Zhou Lab has documented recent high school summer-intern participation, including a 2026 student contributing to ongoing laboratory research. The lab does not advertise a standing high school application process, so prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent inquiry rather than an openly recruiting program.
ratingNote: A strong individual-lab pathway because the Zhou Lab has recently hosted a high school summer intern who contributed to ongoing research. The laboratory works in advanced structural and cellular biology, including techniques such as cryo-electron tomography.
summary: The Zhou Lab at Vanderbilt conducts structural and cellular biology research involving advanced imaging and microscopy approaches, including cryo-electron tomography. The laboratory has recently hosted a high school summer intern who contributed to ongoing research projects, making direct inquiry potentially worthwhile when space and mentorship are available.

name: Research Experience for High School Students (REHSS)
title: Full-Time Vanderbilt Faculty-Mentored Research Internship
department: Collaborative for STEM Education and Outreach
applicationWindow: REHSS serves eligible rising seniors participating in Vanderbilt's ISR program at Stratford STEM Magnet High School, John Overton High School, or Hillsboro High School. Students complete a six-week full-time research internship in a Vanderbilt or VUMC laboratory. Students should review current Vanderbilt CSEO information for future dates and participation requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptionally substantial high school research placement because students spend six weeks working full time in a Vanderbilt or VUMC research laboratory and complete an independent project under a Vanderbilt faculty mentor.
summary: Vanderbilt's Research Experience for High School Students places eligible rising seniors into Vanderbilt or Vanderbilt University Medical Center research laboratories for six weeks of full-time research. Students conduct an independent project under faculty mentorship while gaining experience in fields that can include biology, chemistry, engineering, biomedical science, and other STEM disciplines.

name: School for Science and Math at Vanderbilt — Summer Research III
title: Six-Week Faculty-Mentored Research Placement
department: School for Science and Math at Vanderbilt
applicationWindow: Summer Research III is available to eligible students enrolled in the School for Science and Math at Vanderbilt through Metropolitan Nashville Public Schools. Between junior and senior year, students complete a six-week full-time research internship with a Vanderbilt or VUMC faculty mentor. Access is limited to students participating in SSMV.
ratingNote: A highly substantial research experience because students conduct an individual research project for six weeks under a Vanderbilt or VUMC faculty mentor. Participants maintain a research notebook and present their findings in a poster format to the Vanderbilt research community.
summary: Summer Research III is the capstone research experience for students in Vanderbilt's School for Science and Math. Participants complete a six-week full-time internship with a Vanderbilt or VUMC faculty mentor, conduct an individual research project, document their work in a research notebook, and present their results to the Vanderbilt community.

name: SHIRE — Summer High-School Internships in Research Experiences
title: Paid Vanderbilt Research Apprenticeship
department: Collaborative for STEM Education and Outreach
applicationWindow: SHIRE serves eligible rising juniors and seniors participating in Vanderbilt's ISR program at Stratford STEM Magnet High School, John Overton High School, or Hillsboro High School. Students work with Vanderbilt researchers on active scientific questions. The 2026 program involved approximately 28 hours per week and is now closed. Students should review current CSEO information for future cycles.
ratingNote: A strong paid research pathway because students work directly with Vanderbilt scientists on genuine research questions rather than completing only classroom activities. Research areas have included cancer biology, cell culture, sustainable engineering, water quality, and other STEM topics.
summary: SHIRE is a paid Vanderbilt research experience for eligible high school students participating in the university's ISR pathway. Students work with Vanderbilt scientists on active research questions in areas such as cancer biology, sustainable engineering, cell culture, environmental science, and water quality. Rising seniors may develop individual projects that continue into the fall.

name: Bugs as Materials Summer Internship
title: Microbial Biomaterials Research Internship
applicationWindow: The Bugs as Materials Summer Internship is designed for eligible local high school students. Participants work alongside Carnegie Mellon researchers on projects involving microbial growth, biofilms, biomaterials, and related engineering research. The 2026 application required materials including a transcript, resume, Pennsylvania work permit, short responses, and a reference. Students should review the official program page for future cycles.
ratingNote: An exceptional individual-lab research opportunity because high school students work directly in Carnegie Mellon Engineering research environments on active microbial and biomaterials projects. Prior participants have produced publication-quality data and contributed to scientific publications.
summary: The Bugs as Materials Summer Internship in Carnegie Mellon's Niepa μBiointerface Lab gives local high school students hands-on research experience at the intersection of chemical engineering, microbiology, biomaterials, and materials science. Students work alongside university researchers on projects involving microbes, biofilms, and biologically derived materials.

name: Outreach for Internships in Science (OIS)
title: High School Research Group Laboratory Internship
applicationWindow: OIS serves eligible Pittsburgh Public Schools high school students and focuses on expanding research access for students from groups historically underrepresented in science. Participants are placed into Carnegie Mellon scientific or theoretical laboratories as members of research groups and conclude the experience by presenting their research at a symposium. Students should review current program information for application dates and participating schools.
ratingNote: A substantial research placement because students are embedded directly into Carnegie Mellon scientific and theoretical laboratories as members of active research groups. The program concludes with formal research presentations to university faculty and guests.
summary: Carnegie Mellon's Outreach for Internships in Science places eligible Pittsburgh Public Schools students into active university research groups. Participants may work in biology, chemistry, physics, computational science, or other STEM areas while gaining direct experience with professional research and presenting their work at a final symposium.

name: Intelligent Control Lab
title: Robotics and Reinforcement Learning Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The Intelligent Control Lab has documented high school research participation, including work involving deep reinforcement learning and robotic assembly. The lab does not advertise a standing high school application process, so interested students should treat this as an availability-dependent inquiry rather than an openly recruiting internship.
ratingNote: A highly advanced professor-level research pathway because previous high school work in the lab has involved deep reinforcement learning, robotics, and 3D assembly. However, current high school availability is not guaranteed and depends on faculty and mentor capacity.
summary: Carnegie Mellon's Intelligent Control Lab conducts robotics and artificial-intelligence research involving reinforcement learning, autonomous systems, human-robot interaction, and robotic planning. The lab has documented high school research participation on advanced projects such as deep reinforcement learning for 3D robotic assembly, making direct inquiry potentially worthwhile when mentorship capacity exists.

name: Wood Neuro Research Group
title: Neuroimaging and Biomedical Engineering Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The Wood Neuro Research Group has documented high school intern participation, including a student whose research poster was later accepted to a high school research section of a biomedical engineering conference. The lab does not advertise a standing high school application process, so prospective students should verify current availability directly with the research group.
ratingNote: A particularly strong neuroscience and biomedical engineering pathway because previous high school researchers have contributed work substantial enough to present at a professional scientific conference. Current participation remains dependent on mentor availability and project capacity.
summary: Professor Sossena Wood's Neuro Research Group at Carnegie Mellon studies brain health using neuroimaging, biomedical engineering, and computational methods. The group has previously hosted high school researchers whose work progressed to conference presentation, making direct inquiry potentially valuable when the laboratory has available mentorship.

name: Faculty-Developed High School Research Internships
title: Individual Faculty-Sponsored Research Internship Pathway
department: Leonard Gelfand Center / Faculty Research Labs
applicationWindow: Carnegie Mellon does not operate a university-wide high school research internship application process. However, the Leonard Gelfand Center notes that on rare occasions internships may be developed directly between individual faculty members and high school students. Interested students would need to identify an appropriate faculty member and secure their willingness to develop and supervise a suitable placement.
ratingNote: A valuable hidden pathway because Carnegie Mellon officially acknowledges that individual faculty members can occasionally develop research internships directly with high school students. These placements are rare and highly dependent on faculty interest, project fit, mentorship capacity, and university requirements.
summary: Carnegie Mellon acknowledges that, although high school internships are generally uncommon, individual faculty members may occasionally develop research placements directly with high school students. Students interested in this pathway must identify a relevant professor or laboratory and secure faculty support, with opportunities potentially spanning AI, robotics, engineering, natural sciences, and social science.

name: MYHealth Research Training Program
title: Youth Health Research Co-Researcher Program
applicationWindow: MYHealth serves high school students in Southeast Michigan and is conducted virtually. Students participate as youth co-researchers, working with University of Michigan researchers on adolescent-health questions and real MyVoice survey data. Participants learn research methods, qualitative analysis, interpretation, and scientific communication before presenting their findings. Students should check current U-M Family Medicine information for future recruitment cycles.
ratingNote: A particularly strong social and health-science opportunity because high school students function as co-researchers and analyze real national youth-health data rather than simply attending research workshops. Participants develop research questions, conduct qualitative analysis, interpret findings, and present their work.
summary: MYHealth is an NIH-funded University of Michigan research-training program in which Southeast Michigan high school students work as co-researchers on adolescent-health questions. Students use real MyVoice national survey data, conduct qualitative thematic analysis, interpret results, develop future research directions, and present their findings while receiving mentorship from U-M researchers.

name: Summer Healthcare Experience in Oncology (SHE Oncology)
title: High School Oncology Research Training Program
applicationWindow: SHE Oncology is designed for eligible Michigan high school sophomores and juniors. The 2026 experience included an optional on-campus research bootcamp followed by two weeks of virtual programming. Students completing the program received a $500 stipend. Prospective applicants should check the Rogel Cancer Center's current K-12 program information for future application dates and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: A strong cancer-focused research-training opportunity combining oncology mentorship, genetics activities, research exposure, and a student project. It is less intensive than a full-time faculty-lab placement but provides meaningful exposure to active cancer research and scientific methods.
summary: SHE Oncology introduces Michigan high school students to cancer biology, genetics, biomedical research, and oncology through a combination of research activities, mentorship, patient case-study work, and hands-on genetics experiences. Participants receive at-home laboratory materials and learn about cancer research through the University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center.

name: MYHealth Peer Leaders
title: Advanced Youth Health Research and Peer Mentorship
applicationWindow: This advanced pathway is available to returning students who have previously completed the MYHealth research-training experience.
