Selected alumni can continue for an additional year as peer leaders, gaining further research experience while helping mentor newer student research teams. Eligibility therefore requires prior participation in MYHealth.
ratingNote: A valuable long-term research pathway for returning MYHealth participants because students can extend their involvement into a second year while developing both research and scientific mentorship experience.
summary: MYHealth alumni can continue their involvement with University of Michigan health research as peer leaders. Returning students gain additional research experience while mentoring newer participants as they develop and complete youth-health research projects, allowing some students to spend roughly two years progressing through research and mentorship.

name: Health Sciences Pre-College Exposure Academy (SPEA)
title: Biomedical and Health Sciences Summer Experience
applicationWindow: SPEA is available to eligible U.S. high school sophomores and juniors with at least a 3.0 GPA. The program includes professional-development programming and weekly full-day experiences at Michigan Medicine for students interested in medicine, biomedical research, health sciences, and health equity. Applicants should review the current Michigan Medicine K-12 Pathways page for application dates and requirements.
ratingNote: A useful introduction to biomedical research and Michigan Medicine, particularly for students exploring medicine and health equity. However, this should be viewed primarily as research and healthcare exposure rather than an independent faculty-lab research placement.
summary: The Health Sciences Pre-College Exposure Academy introduces high school students to medicine, biomedical research, health sciences, and health equity through programming connected to Michigan Medicine. Participants attend professional-development sessions and full-day campus experiences while exploring research and healthcare careers.

name: Rogel Cancer Center K-12 Research Pathways / TrECC
title: High School Cancer Research Pathways
applicationWindow: Eligibility and application timing vary by the individual K-12 research and training opportunities offered through the Rogel Cancer Center and its training infrastructure. Students should use the current Rogel trainee resources to identify programs appropriate for their grade level, location, and research interests.
ratingNote: Useful as a specialized access point for students seeking cancer and oncology research opportunities at the University of Michigan, although it functions more as a pathway to individual programs than as one standalone research internship.
summary: The University of Michigan Rogel Cancer Center supports K-12 pathways that introduce high school students to cancer biology, oncology, biomedical science, and translational research. Opportunities vary by program and can include research training, mentorship, scientific projects, and exposure to the cancer-research environment at Michigan Medicine.

name: High School Research Internship
title: Academic-Year Faculty-Lab Research Internship
applicationWindow: The High School Research Internship serves eligible local high school juniors and seniors through participating schools and community organizations. Students conduct research in a Notre Dame faculty laboratory approximately twice per week during the academic year while working closely with a graduate student or postdoctoral mentor. Participants complete a research project and present their work at a poster presentation.
ratingNote: An exceptionally substantial academic-year research experience because students are embedded directly in Notre Dame faculty laboratories and work with graduate student or postdoctoral mentors. The program has placed dozens of high school students across numerous Notre Dame research labs.
summary: Notre Dame's High School Research Internship places local juniors and seniors into university faculty laboratories for sustained academic-year research. Students work closely with graduate student or postdoctoral mentors, contribute to research projects across STEM disciplines, and conclude the experience by presenting their work in a research poster.

name: CISTAR Young Scholars Program
title: Paid Chemical Engineering Research Internship
applicationWindow: The CISTAR Young Scholars Program is designed for eligible rising juniors, rising seniors, and graduating high school seniors who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents. Priority is given to students in the Notre Dame area. The 2026 program ran June 15 through July 24, with students conducting research approximately 30 hours per week in CISTAR-affiliated laboratories and receiving a $2,000 stipend. Students should check the current program page for future application cycles.
ratingNote: A highly substantial engineering research opportunity because high school students spend six weeks conducting full-time research inside CISTAR-affiliated Notre Dame laboratories. The combination of intensive laboratory work, faculty research, and a stipend makes this one of Notre Dame's strongest high school STEM opportunities.
summary: The CISTAR Young Scholars Program gives high school students six weeks of intensive research experience in Notre Dame laboratories connected to chemical engineering, chemistry, catalysis, energy, and sustainable engineering. Participants work approximately 30 hours per week on active research and receive a stipend.

name: Summer Research Experience for High School Students
title: Chemistry and Biochemistry Faculty-Lab Research
applicationWindow: Notre Dame's Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry offers a Summer Research Experience in which high school students may perform research in faculty laboratories. Interested students are directed by the department to contact Professor Greg Hartland for information about available projects. Participation therefore depends on current project and mentorship availability.
ratingNote: An excellent department-level direct-inquiry pathway because Notre Dame explicitly invites interested high school students to ask about available research projects in Chemistry and Biochemistry faculty laboratories rather than relying on an unofficial cold-email strategy.
summary: Notre Dame Chemistry and Biochemistry offers high school students opportunities to conduct summer research in university faculty laboratories. Projects can span chemistry, biochemistry, molecular science, and chemical biology, with interested students directed to inquire about currently available research projects.

name: Research Experience for High School Students — Environmental Engineering
title: Doudrick Lab Environmental Engineering Research
department: Civil and Environmental Engineering and Earth Sciences
applicationWindow: Notre Dame's academic catalog lists CE 08999, Research Experience for High School Students, as an Environmental Engineering research experience associated with Professor Kyle Doudrick. Participation requires an appropriate research project and faculty approval rather than a standard centralized high school application.
ratingNote: An unusually strong individual-professor pathway because Notre Dame formally recognizes a course specifically for high school students conducting Environmental Engineering research. The opportunity provides a route into research involving environmental contaminants, water treatment, and related environmental engineering questions.
summary: Notre Dame formally lists a Research Experience for High School Students in Environmental Engineering associated with Professor Kyle Doudrick. Research in this area can involve environmental contaminants, PFAS, environmental chemistry, and water-treatment technologies, providing an unusually specific faculty-level pathway for high school research.

name: Research Cures Cancer Corps (RC3) Summer Immersion
title: High School Cancer Research Laboratory Experience
applicationWindow: The RC3 Summer Immersion provides high school students with hands-on cancer research experience associated with the Harper Cancer Research Institute. Participants work alongside research mentors in affiliated laboratories on cancer research projects. Students should consult current Notre Dame and Harper Cancer Research Institute information for future program dates and application requirements.
ratingNote: A highly valuable biomedical research experience because high school participants work alongside research mentors on actual cancer research projects in laboratories affiliated with Notre Dame's Harper Cancer Research Institute.
summary: The Research Cures Cancer Corps Summer Immersion introduces high school students to hands-on cancer research at Notre Dame. Participants work with mentors in Harper Cancer Research Institute-affiliated laboratories on projects involving cancer biology, molecular biology, biomedical science, and oncology.

name: Summer Focus — Young Scientist Program
title: Paid Individual Laboratory Research Internship
applicationWindow: Summer Focus is designed for eligible Greater St. Louis-area high school juniors entering their senior year who reside in Missouri or Illinois. Students spend approximately eight weeks conducting full-time research in a Washington University laboratory under scientist mentorship. The 2026 program provided a $4,800 stipend. No previous research experience is expected. Students should check the Young Scientist Program website for future application dates.
ratingNote: An exceptional high school research experience because each participant completes an individualized project inside an active Washington University laboratory. Students work full-time with scientist mentors and conclude the experience by presenting their research at a symposium.
summary: Summer Focus places Greater St. Louis-area high school students into Washington University research laboratories for approximately eight weeks of full-time mentored research. Students complete individualized projects in areas that can include genetics, cancer biology, neuroscience, microbiology, biomedical engineering, ecology, chemistry, and other STEM fields before presenting their work at a final symposium.

name: CRISPr — Cancer Research Inspiring Future Scientists Program
title: Paid Cancer Research Laboratory Internship
department: Siteman Cancer Center / Department of Biology
applicationWindow: CRISPr serves eligible St. Louis-area high school students who are at least 16 years old and eligible to work in the United States. Participants spend approximately nine weeks conducting full-time cancer research with mentors in Washington University Medicine laboratories. The program has provided a $4,800 stipend. Information for the 2027 cycle is expected in December 2026.
ratingNote: An exceptionally intensive cancer-research opportunity because high school students spend roughly 40 hours per week working in cancer research laboratories with scientist mentors. Participants also develop scientific reading and presentation skills and present their work at a research symposium.
summary: The Cancer Research Inspiring Future Scientists Program places St. Louis-area high school students into cancer research laboratories at Washington University Medicine. Participants spend approximately nine weeks working with research mentors on cancer-related projects while developing scientific communication skills and presenting their findings at a final symposium.

name: Blodgett Lab
title: Microbiology and Bacterial Metabolism Research Opportunity
applicationWindow: The Blodgett Lab has a documented history of hosting high school researchers, generally from schools in the St. Louis area. High school positions depend on laboratory funding and mentorship availability. The lab currently states that no high school positions are open, so students should verify current availability before reaching out and should not assume that a placement is available.
ratingNote: A strong individual faculty-lab pathway because the Blodgett Lab explicitly recognizes high school researchers and has hosted multiple students. Unlike a general summer program, students may gain experience directly within an active microbiology research group, although positions are highly availability dependent.
summary: The Blodgett Lab at Washington University studies microbiology, bacterial metabolism, biochemistry, and related areas of chemical biology. The laboratory has previously hosted several high school researchers, particularly students from the St. Louis area. Opportunities depend on funding and mentor capacity, and the lab currently reports no open high school positions.

name: Center for Women's Infectious Disease Research — High School Research
title: High School Infectious Disease Research Pathway
department: Center for Women's Infectious Disease Research
applicationWindow: The Center for Women's Infectious Disease Research maintains information specifically for high school students seeking research experiences and directs students toward Washington University pathways offering summer or school-year research projects. Availability and eligibility depend on the specific program or placement, so students should review the center's current high school research information before applying.
ratingNote: A useful specialized research-access pathway for high school students interested in infectious disease, microbiology, immunology, and women's health. It is best understood as an entry point to WashU high school research opportunities rather than a single guaranteed laboratory internship.
summary: Washington University's Center for Women's Infectious Disease Research provides a pathway for high school students interested in infectious disease and biomedical research to identify summer and academic-year research opportunities. Students can explore research connected to microbiology, immunology, women's health, and related biomedical fields through WashU's broader high school research infrastructure.

name: Young Scientist Program — Continuing Mentoring
title: Multi-Year High School Scientist Mentorship
applicationWindow: Continuing Mentoring serves students in grades 9 through 12 at participating St. Louis schools, including Soldan International Studies High School and the Collegiate School of Medicine and Bioscience. Students are paired with Washington University graduate student mentors and meet throughout high school for science activities and individualized academic and professional development.
ratingNote: A useful long-term research-preparation pathway because students can develop sustained relationships with Washington University graduate scientist mentors throughout high school. It is less intensive than a direct laboratory internship such as Summer Focus or CRISPr, so it should be viewed primarily as scientific mentorship and research preparation.
summary: The Young Scientist Program's Continuing Mentoring pathway pairs participating St. Louis high school students with Washington University graduate student scientists. Students meet regularly throughout high school for science activities, individualized mentorship, academic development, and preparation for future STEM and research opportunities.

name: NextGen High School Internship Program
title: Paid Human Genetics and Biomedical Research Internship
applicationWindow: The NextGen High School Internship Program provides eligible high school students, with an Atlanta-area focus, with a paid summer experience through Emory's Department of Human Genetics. The program returned in 2026 after pausing in 2025. Participants receive hands-on exposure to genetics research, laboratory techniques, scientific careers, and genetic counseling. Students should review the current Human Genetics program page for future application dates and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional biomedical research opportunity because high school students gain hands-on experience across Emory research environments while working with researchers in human genetics and related fields. Recent participants have explored techniques involving leukemia-cell mutations, fruit-fly genetics, and induced pluripotent stem cells.
summary: Emory's NextGen High School Internship Program gives high school students a paid, hands-on introduction to human genetics and biomedical research. Participants work with Emory researchers, develop laboratory and scientific skills, explore areas such as molecular biology, neuroscience and stem-cell research, and learn about careers including genetic counseling.

name: Faculty-Sponsored Minor Research Laboratory Placement
title: Individual Faculty-Sponsored Research Lab Pathway
applicationWindow: Emory has an administrative process for minors participating in university research laboratories. This is not a centralized high school internship program. A student must first have a willing Emory PI, supervisor, or laboratory contact who agrees to sponsor the research experience. The minor must then complete applicable university registration, safety training, and laboratory requirements before participating.
ratingNote: A valuable hidden pathway because Emory has an established administrative mechanism for minors to participate in university research laboratories when supported by a willing PI or lab supervisor. Placement is highly dependent on faculty interest, laboratory capacity, project suitability, and university approval.
summary: High school students can potentially conduct research in individual Emory laboratories when a faculty PI or laboratory supervisor agrees to sponsor them. Emory maintains procedures for minors entering research laboratories, including registration and required safety training, creating an official pathway for individually arranged faculty-sponsored research experiences.

name: Summer Science Academy
title: Biomedical Science and Research Exposure Program
applicationWindow: The Summer Science Academy is designed for incoming ninth- and tenth-grade students interested in science and medicine. The two-week experience includes hands-on laboratory and field activities connected to biotechnology, medical and scientific research, engineering, and health careers. The program is on hiatus for summer 2026 and is expected to return in summer 2027, so students should verify the next cycle before applying.
ratingNote: A useful opportunity for younger high school students to gain hands-on exposure to biomedical science and university research environments. It is primarily a research-exposure and science-enrichment experience rather than an independent faculty-lab research internship.
summary: Emory School of Medicine's Summer Science Academy introduces younger high school students to biomedical science through hands-on laboratory and field experiences. Students explore biotechnology, medical research, engineering, health science, and related careers while gaining early exposure to the scientific research environment.

name: Foundations of Modern Biology II Laboratory
title: College-Credit Authentic Biology Research Laboratory
applicationWindow: Eligible high school students who have completed their sophomore or junior year and meet applicable prerequisites may enroll through Emory Summer College. The laboratory is conducted on campus and requires students to be local to Atlanta during the session. Students design, implement, analyze, and present authentic research projects while earning Emory college credit. Unlike many Research Connect listings, this is tuition-based coursework rather than a free or paid internship.
ratingNote: A legitimate authentic-research experience because students design, conduct, analyze, and present their own experimental biology projects. However, it is a tuition-based college laboratory course rather than a competitive research internship or individual faculty-lab placement.
summary: Foundations of Modern Biology II Laboratory allows eligible high school students enrolled through Emory Summer College to participate in authentic experimental biology research. Students design and implement research projects, analyze their results, present their findings, and earn Emory college credit through the laboratory course.

name: Emory Pre-Med Institute
title: Research and Health Sciences Pre-Med Experience
applicationWindow: The Emory Pre-Med Institute is designed for eligible rising high school juniors and seniors. The three-week program provides intensive exposure to medicine, biomedical science, health research, and healthcare careers with involvement from Emory School of Medicine faculty. The 2026 program reached capacity early. Students should review Emory's current Pre-College information for future sessions and application requirements.
ratingNote: A useful medical and biomedical-science exposure experience, but substantially less research-intensive than Emory's NextGen internship or an individual faculty-sponsored laboratory placement. It should be treated as research and healthcare exposure rather than independent research.
summary: The Emory Pre-Med Institute is a three-week summer experience for rising juniors and seniors interested in medicine and biomedical science. Students explore clinical and research careers in health care through programming connected to Emory and its School of Medicine, making it primarily an introductory research and medical-science experience.

name: Tong Lab
title: High School Volunteer Research Internship
applicationWindow: The Tong Lab explicitly invites high school students interested in possible volunteer research internships to contact Dr. YuYe Tong directly. High school applicants are asked to provide a personal statement, CV, and two recommendation letters. Selected applicants may be invited for an on-site interview, and accepted minors must complete applicable parental-consent and university requirements. Opportunities depend on laboratory availability.
ratingNote: An exceptional individual-lab pathway because the Tong Lab explicitly provides a research-internship application route for high school students rather than requiring students to rely on unsolicited cold outreach. Successful students can gain direct experience within an active Georgetown chemistry research environment.
summary: The Tong Lab at Georgetown University explicitly welcomes inquiries from high school students interested in volunteer research internships. Students can apply directly to Dr. YuYe Tong for opportunities involving analytical chemistry, environmental chemistry, environmental metrology, and related laboratory research.

name: Evidence for Justice Lab
title: High School Research Assistant
applicationWindow: The Evidence for Justice Lab explicitly accepts applications from high school, undergraduate, and graduate students interested in joining its research team. The lab provides a direct research-assistant application pathway and currently identifies Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 recruitment cycles. Applicants should review the current recruitment page for deadlines and cohort availability.
ratingNote: An unusually strong high school social-science research opportunity because students can directly apply to join an active Georgetown research team. The lab's work provides exposure to evidence-based justice reform, social-science research, policy questions, and research methodology.
summary: Georgetown's Evidence for Justice Lab explicitly allows high school students to apply to join its research team. Research assistants contribute to projects examining criminal justice and evidence-based justice reform, creating a rare university-level social-science research pathway for high school students.

name: High School Summer Research Volunteer Program
title: Full-Time Cancer Research Internship
applicationWindow: The High School Summer Research Volunteer Program provides high school students with approximately eight weeks of full-time research at Georgetown's Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. Students work about 40 hours per week under research-scientist mentorship and conduct independent research projects. The 2026 program ran June 22 through August 14, with applications closing March 31. Students should check the current Lombardi program page for future application cycles.
ratingNote: An exceptionally intensive biomedical research opportunity because participants spend roughly eight weeks working full-time on independent cancer research projects under scientist mentorship at a comprehensive cancer center.
summary: Georgetown's Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center offers high school students an intensive summer research experience in cancer and biomedical science. Participants spend approximately eight weeks working full-time with research scientists while completing independent research projects in an active cancer-research environment.

name: AI CoLab AI in Healthcare Internship
title: Applied Artificial Intelligence and Healthcare Research Internship
department: AI CoLab / Georgetown University Medical Center / MedStar Health
applicationWindow: The AI CoLab summer internship explicitly includes high school students among eligible applicants. The in-person program lasts approximately nine to twelve weeks and involves applied AI and healthcare research using publicly available data. Interns can participate in research-question development, data analysis, interpretation, and dissemination while gaining exposure to machine learning, clinical informatics, bioinformatics, biostatistics, and research operations. Students should verify current application dates and eligibility before applying.
ratingNote: A particularly strong interdisciplinary opportunity because high school students can participate in actual AI and healthcare research rather than simply completing an introductory coding course. The combination of data analysis, research development, and scientific dissemination makes this highly relevant for students interested in AI, medicine, or computational research.
summary: Georgetown and MedStar's AI CoLab offers high school students an applied summer research internship at the intersection of artificial intelligence and healthcare. Interns work with data and contribute to stages of the research process while exploring machine learning, bioinformatics, biostatistics, clinical informatics, and medical research.

name: Gateway Exploration Program
title: High School Medical Department Internship and Mentorship
applicationWindow: The Gateway Exploration Program serves eligible rising high school sophomores, juniors, and seniors through participating school systems. Historically focused on DC Public Schools, the program expanded in 2026 to include scholars from Prince William County Public Schools in Virginia. Students are matched with Georgetown medical departments and participate in mentorship, shadowing, professional-development activities, and programming related to health disparities. Students should verify current participating school systems and eligibility for future cycles.
ratingNote: A meaningful Georgetown medical experience involving department placement, mentorship, and exposure to healthcare and health disparities. However, it is primarily a clinical and medical-exposure opportunity rather than an independent research internship, making it less research-intensive than Georgetown's Lombardi, Tong Lab, or AI CoLab opportunities.
summary: Georgetown School of Medicine's Gateway Exploration Program introduces eligible high school students to medicine and health science through medical-department placements, mentorship, shadowing, professional development, and health-disparities programming. It provides valuable medical exposure, although it is not primarily an independent research program.

name: Linnstaedt Lab
title: Neuroscience and Chronic Pain Research Opportunity
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
department: School of Medicine / Department of Anesthesiology
applicationWindow: The Linnstaedt Lab has documented prior high school research participation, including a high school research assistant mentored over multiple years. The lab does not advertise a standing high school application process, so prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent inquiry and verify current mentorship capacity before reaching out.
ratingNote: A strong individual-lab pathway because the Linnstaedt Lab has documented sustained high school research participation in an active biomedical research environment. Current opportunities are not guaranteed and depend on faculty, mentor, and project availability.
summary: The Linnstaedt Lab at UNC School of Medicine studies molecular and genetic mechanisms involved in trauma, chronic pain, and related neurological outcomes. The group has previously hosted a high school research assistant, making direct inquiry potentially worthwhile for students interested in neuroscience, genetics, molecular biology, and computational approaches to biomedical research.

name: Griffith Lab
title: Computational Medicine and Cardiovascular Modeling Research Opportunity
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
applicationWindow: Professor Boyce Griffith has previously mentored a high school student in summer research, providing evidence that high school participation has occurred in the research group. There is no standing high school application page, so any current placement would depend on faculty interest, project suitability, and mentorship availability.
ratingNote: An unusually advanced computational research pathway because the group works at the intersection of applied mathematics, scientific computing, computational biology, and cardiovascular modeling. Prior high school mentorship is documented, although current openings are unconfirmed.
summary: The Griffith research group at UNC works on computational and experimental modeling of cardiovascular systems using applied mathematics and scientific computing. Professor Boyce Griffith has previously mentored a high school researcher, making this a potential direct-inquiry pathway for students interested in mathematical biology, simulation, and computational medicine.

name: UNC Faculty-Sponsored Unpaid Research Internship Pathway
title: Individual Faculty-Sponsored High School Research Internship
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
applicationWindow: UNC administrative materials recognize high school students as potential unpaid interns participating in experiential learning under university supervision. This is not a centralized high school research program. Students would need to identify an appropriate UNC faculty member or supervisor willing to support an individually arranged placement, subject to university requirements and approvals.
ratingNote: A valuable hidden pathway because UNC has an administrative framework that can support supervised high school internships. It provides institutional evidence that individually arranged research placements may be possible when a student secures an appropriate faculty sponsor.
summary: UNC-Chapel Hill has an administrative pathway that can support high school students participating in supervised unpaid internships, including research-oriented experiences arranged with faculty or university supervisors. Students must independently identify a suitable mentor and secure sponsorship, making this a direct-inquiry pathway rather than a centralized application program.

name: Redinbo Lab
title: Chemistry, Structural Biology and Microbiome Research Opportunity
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
applicationWindow: Professor Matthew Redinbo has documented prior mentorship of high school students, including summer research participation in his group. The available evidence is historical rather than a current recruitment announcement, so interested students should verify whether the lab currently has suitable projects and mentorship capacity before reaching out.
ratingNote: A strong individual chemistry and biochemistry lab pathway because the research group has previously hosted high school students in summer research. Current participation is not guaranteed and should be treated as availability dependent.
summary: The Redinbo Lab at UNC conducts research spanning chemistry, biochemistry, structural biology, chemical biology, and the microbiome. Professor Matthew Redinbo has previously mentored high school researchers, making the lab a possible direct-inquiry option when suitable projects and mentor availability exist.

name: UNC Chemistry High School Research Mentorship Pathway
title: Faculty-Supervised High School Chemistry Research
university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
applicationWindow: UNC Chemistry has documented faculty mentorship of local high school students who developed and carried out research projects using university equipment, chemicals, and scientific guidance. The evidence is historical rather than a current centralized application program, so participation should be considered faculty- and availability-dependent.
ratingNote: A meaningful chemistry research pathway because high school students have previously developed and carried out their own projects with UNC faculty support and access to university research resources. Current opportunities depend on faculty willingness and project availability.
summary: UNC Chemistry has previously supported local high school students in faculty-supervised research projects involving experimental design, laboratory work, scientific discussion, and access to university equipment and materials. This pathway is best treated as an individual faculty-contact opportunity rather than a currently open structured program.

name: Jomaa Lab
title: Cell Biology and Structural Biology Research Opportunity
department: School of Medicine / Department of Molecular Physiology and Biological Physics
applicationWindow: The Jomaa Lab has documented Grade 10 high school interns in both 2024 and 2025. The lab does not advertise a standing high school application process, so prospective students should treat this as an availability-dependent opportunity and verify current mentorship capacity before reaching out.
ratingNote: An exceptional individual-lab pathway because the Jomaa Lab has hosted high school interns in consecutive recent years. Students may gain exposure to advanced cell and structural biology research, although current positions are not guaranteed.
summary: The Jomaa Lab at the University of Virginia School of Medicine studies cellular mechanisms involved in protein targeting to the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria, as well as cellular dormancy in health and disease. The lab has hosted Grade 10 high school interns in both 2024 and 2025, providing unusually recent evidence that high school participation is possible.

name: Summer Opportunities in Academic Research (SOAR)
title: High School Biomedical Research Program
applicationWindow: SOAR has operated as an eight-week research experience for Charlottesville-area high school students, pairing participants with UVA research mentors and providing exposure to biomedical laboratory research. Current-cycle availability should be verified because the latest detailed UVA program documentation is historical rather than a confirmed 2026 application announcement.
ratingNote: A substantial structured biomedical research experience involving direct mentorship and exposure to active UVA research laboratories. Current program availability should be confirmed before applying.
summary: Summer Opportunities in Academic Research introduces Charlottesville-area high school students to biomedical and translational research at UVA. Participants are paired with research mentors and gain direct experience with university research, including laboratory-based projects in areas such as cancer and biomedical science.

name: Charlottesville City of Promise × UVA Chemical Engineering Research Experience
title: High School Chemical Engineering Research Experience
applicationWindow: This partnership has provided local Charlottesville high school students with a four-week research experience in UVA Chemical Engineering laboratories through City of Promise. The documented cohort received $1,000 stipends. Because the available official documentation describes an earlier cohort, students should verify whether the partnership is currently offering placements.
ratingNote: A strong community-based university research experience involving active UVA laboratories, graduate-student mentorship, and compensated participation. Current availability depends on continuation of the City of Promise partnership.
summary: Through a partnership between Charlottesville City of Promise and UVA Chemical Engineering, local high school students have spent four weeks working in university laboratories on active research with graduate-student mentors and faculty support. The documented program provided students with $1,000 stipends for their participation.

name: Link Lab — Charlottesville High School Mentorship Program
title: Engineering Research and Project Mentorship Program
department: Link Lab / School of Engineering and Applied Science
applicationWindow: Participation is through the Charlottesville High School Engineering program rather than a general public application. During the 2025-26 program, Link Lab mentors worked with CHS students on semester-long engineering projects and provided technical guidance, project-management support, and exposure to UVA Engineering research spaces.
ratingNote: A meaningful long-term engineering mentorship experience with UVA researchers and access to the university's engineering environment. It is more project- and design-focused than an independent faculty research internship.
summary: The UVA Link Lab partners with Charlottesville High School to mentor students through semester-long engineering projects. Students receive technical and project-development guidance from UVA mentors while gaining exposure to engineering laboratories, research spaces, robotics, cyber-physical systems, and university-level engineering work.

name: Emerging Engineers
title: UVA Engineering High School Summer Program
department: School of Engineering and Applied Science
applicationWindow: The 2026 Emerging Engineers program runs July 27-31 and is open to rising students in grades 9-12. The program is free and includes hands-on engineering activities, laboratory exposure, interaction with UVA researchers, and specialized tracks including Biomedical Engineering and Materials Science & Engineering.
ratingNote: A useful free introduction to university engineering and research environments, particularly for younger high school students. It provides hands-on activities and research exposure but is not equivalent to an independent laboratory research internship.
summary: Emerging Engineers is a free UVA summer program for rising high school students interested in engineering. Participants complete hands-on activities, interact with UVA researchers, visit university research environments, and explore specialized areas including biomedical engineering and materials science and engineering.

name: Young Researchers Program (YRP)
title: High School STEM Research Program
department: USC Dornsife College of Letters, Arts and Sciences
applicationWindow: The 2026 Young Researchers Program application cycle is closed and acceptances have been sent. The next application cycle is expected in early 2027. Participants should be rising high school seniors and must be able to commit at least 15 hours per week to their research project during the six-week program.
ratingNote: A strong university-level research experience because students spend six weeks working on scientific projects with USC research mentors and conclude by presenting their work at a research poster symposium.
summary: USC Dornsife's Young Researchers Program gives rising high school seniors the opportunity to conduct university-level STEM research with USC mentors. Students spend at least 15 hours per week on their research projects while also participating in seminars, field trips, and scientific-development activities before presenting their work at a final poster symposium.

name: SHINE
title: USC Viterbi High School Engineering Research Program
applicationWindow: SHINE is a seven-week summer research experience for high school students through USC Viterbi. Students are placed with USC faculty research teams and participate in laboratory or computational research. Students should verify the current application dates and eligibility requirements on the official SHINE program page.
ratingNote: One of USC's strongest high school engineering opportunities because participants join faculty research teams and contribute to hands-on laboratory or computational research on real engineering problems.
summary: SHINE gives high school students seven weeks of hands-on research experience with USC Viterbi faculty teams. Research can span artificial intelligence, robotics, biomedical engineering, computer science, materials science, environmental engineering, and other engineering fields, with students contributing to laboratory or computational projects.

name: Wang Lab
title: 2D Materials and Nanotechnology Research through SHINE
department: Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering
applicationWindow: High school participation in Professor Han Wang's research group occurs through USC Viterbi's SHINE program rather than through a separate Wang Lab high school application. The lab states that it participates in SHINE each summer and has hosted high school students conducting research on 2D materials.
ratingNote: An unusually specific faculty-lab pathway for high school students, with documented participation in advanced nanotechnology and 2D-materials research. Admission is through the competitive SHINE program.
summary: Professor Han Wang's USC research group participates in the SHINE program and hosts high school researchers working on advanced electrical engineering and materials-science projects. Previous high school participants have conducted laboratory research involving two-dimensional materials and produced research posters documenting their work.

name: Bridge Undergraduate Science Program Junior (BUGS Jr.)
title: High School Interdisciplinary Biomedical Research Program
applicationWindow: USC identifies BUGS Jr. through the Bridge Institute as a research opportunity for high school students. Students interested in participating should verify the current program schedule, eligibility requirements, and application process through USC and the Bridge Institute.
ratingNote: A distinctive interdisciplinary science opportunity connected to USC's Bridge Institute, particularly useful for students interested in combining biology, chemistry, computation, and medicine.
summary: BUGS Jr. is a high school research pathway associated with USC's Bridge Institute and its interdisciplinary approach to understanding the human body. The program exposes students to research spanning structural biology, biochemistry, computational biology, biomedical science, and related molecular sciences.

name: Music and the Brain Summer Research Program
title: High School Neuroscience and Music Cognition Research Program
applicationWindow: The 2026 Music and the Brain Summer Research Program ran July 8-10 for students in grades 10-12. The program accepted up to 80 students and cost $500, with financial assistance available. Students should check the Brain and Creativity Institute for information about future program cycles.
ratingNote: A distinctive neuroscience and psychology research-exposure opportunity involving scientific data collection and interaction with USC researchers, although it is much shorter and less independent than a full research internship.
summary: USC's Music and the Brain Summer Research Program introduces high school students to neuroscience, psychology, and music cognition. Participants explore how music affects the brain through guided research activities, laboratory experiences, interaction with USC researchers, and hands-on scientific data collection.

name: Komor Lab
title: High School Genome Editing Research Internship
applicationWindow: The Komor Lab explicitly provides a dedicated application pathway for high school students seeking research internships. Interested students should use the high school internship application linked on the lab's Join page and verify current availability before applying.
ratingNote: An exceptional individual-lab opportunity because the Komor Lab directly invites high school internship applications rather than merely documenting past high school researchers. The lab conducts advanced genome-editing and chemical-biology research.
summary: The Komor Lab at UC San Diego develops and studies genome-editing technologies at the intersection of chemistry, biology, and genetics. High school students have a dedicated internship application pathway, making this a rare opportunity to directly seek research experience in an individual university laboratory working on CRISPR and related genome-engineering technologies.

name: Cardiovascular Institute Summer Research Program
title: High School Cardiovascular Research Internship
applicationWindow: The 2026 application deadline was March 31. Rising high school juniors and seniors age 16 or older are eligible for the eight-week summer program. High school participants receive a $2,500 stipend. Students should check the Cardiovascular Institute website for the next application cycle.
ratingNote: A highly substantial paid biomedical research experience combining eight weeks of research, mentorship from UC San Diego clinician-scientists, research training, lectures, and exposure to clinical medicine.
summary: UC San Diego's Cardiovascular Institute Summer Research Program provides rising high school juniors and seniors with an eight-week research experience in cardiovascular science. Participants receive mentorship from clinician-scientists, research training, lectures, clinical exposure, and a $2,500 stipend.

name: Research Immersion in Materials Science and Engineering (RIMSE)
title: High School Materials Science Research Program
department: Materials Research Science and Engineering Center
applicationWindow: Local high school students interested in RIMSE must contact an eligible UC San Diego MRSEC faculty researcher before applying, establish mutual research interests, secure a mentor, and develop a proposed Discovery research project. The 2026 high school application deadline was March 15. MRSEC funding is not available for high school participants.
ratingNote: An unusually strong pathway because students proactively connect with a UC San Diego faculty researcher and develop an independent materials-science research project under mentorship over approximately eight to ten weeks.
summary: RIMSE allows a select number of local high school students to conduct materials-science and engineering research with UC San Diego MRSEC faculty. Students first identify and contact a potential faculty mentor, establish shared research interests, and formulate an independent Discovery project before applying to the program.

name: BE-SHIP
title: Bioengineering Scholar High School Internship Project
applicationWindow: Students progress through required Bioengineering Research Scholars preparation before undertaking BE-SHIP research. The pathway allows advanced students to develop an individual bioengineering research project in collaboration with a university laboratory and may lead to an on-site summer internship. Fall 2026 BERP-A is listed for grades 9-12 with a September 18 application deadline.
ratingNote: A substantial research pathway because students can independently propose, execute, analyze, and present a bioengineering project in collaboration with a university research laboratory, with advanced work potentially developing toward abstracts, science fairs, or manuscripts.
summary: BE-SHIP gives prepared high school students the opportunity to develop and carry out individual bioengineering research projects in collaboration with university laboratories. Projects may involve areas such as bioimaging, tissue engineering, biomechanics, and biomedical engineering, with students progressing through experimental work, analysis, and scientific presentation.

name: OPALS High School Internship
title: Engineering in Medicine Research Internship
applicationWindow: Applications for the Spring 2027 OPALS High School Internship are scheduled to open September 27, 2026. Students should verify the final application deadline and eligibility requirements through UC San Diego's Institute of Engineering in Medicine.
ratingNote: A strong interdisciplinary research internship combining engineering, medicine, artificial intelligence, and data science. Students contribute to research activities and conclude their experience with a scientific presentation or poster.
summary: The OPALS High School Internship at UC San Diego's Institute of Engineering in Medicine places students alongside researchers, graduate students, and industry collaborators working on interdisciplinary projects involving engineering, medicine, AI, and data science. Students work with scientific data, evaluate experimental results, contribute to ongoing research efforts, and finish with a research presentation or poster.

name: Student Science Training Program (SSTP)
title: High School Faculty-Lab Research Program
department: Center for Precollegiate Education and Training
applicationWindow: The 2026 Student Science Training Program ran June 7-July 25. The seven-week residential program is designed for rising 12th graders, with students from outside Florida also eligible for a limited number of positions. Students should check the official SSTP page for the next application cycle.
ratingNote: One of the University of Florida's strongest high school research opportunities because students spend seven weeks working with a UF faculty research scientist and research team on ongoing university research.
summary: The Student Science Training Program is a seven-week residential research experience for rising high school seniors. Participants are placed with University of Florida faculty research scientists and research teams, where they contribute to ongoing research across areas such as biology, medicine, chemistry, engineering, and computer science.

name: Kenan Fellows High School Summer Internship
title: High School Biomedical Research Internship
department: The Herbert Wertheim UF Scripps Institute for Biomedical Innovation & Technology
applicationWindow: The Kenan Fellows program is available to eligible high school students from Palm Beach and Martin counties. Participants spend eight weeks working approximately 40 hours per week in a Wertheim UF Scripps research laboratory and receive a $4,480 stipend. Students should check the official program page for the next application cycle and current eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: An exceptional paid biomedical research experience involving eight weeks of full-time laboratory work, experimental design, bench research, data analysis, and direct mentorship from scientists at a major biomedical research institute.
summary: The Kenan Fellows High School Summer Internship places Palm Beach and Martin County students in biomedical research laboratories at the Wertheim UF Scripps Institute. Students spend eight weeks conducting full-time research under scientific mentorship while learning research planning, experimental design, laboratory techniques, and data analysis.

name: Research Immersion in Science & Engineering (RISE)
title: High School Science and Engineering Research Immersion
department: Center for Precollegiate Education and Training
applicationWindow: RISE is designed for rising 10th-grade students. The 2026 program offered a one-week research immersion involving laboratory activities, case studies, research-focused experiences, and interaction with University of Florida researchers. A limited number of spaces may be available to students from outside Florida.
ratingNote: A useful early high school research experience because rising sophomores can gain laboratory and research exposure at UF. It is an immersion program rather than an independent faculty-lab research internship.
summary: Research Immersion in Science & Engineering introduces rising high school sophomores to scientific and engineering research at the University of Florida. Students participate in laboratory experiments, hands-on research activities, case studies, research-focused field experiences, and discussions with faculty and graduate researchers.

name: Research Explorations (REx)
title: Advanced High School Research Program
department: Center for Precollegiate Education and Training
applicationWindow: Research Explorations is designed for rising 11th- and 12th-grade students and offers advanced research experiences in biomedical science or environmental science and toxicology. Students from outside Florida may apply for a limited number of spaces. Need-based scholarships may be available to qualifying Florida students.
ratingNote: A strong research-training experience involving advanced laboratory techniques and interaction with UF researchers. It provides more substantial scientific training than a typical pre-college enrichment program, although it is not an independent faculty-lab internship.
summary: Research Explorations is a two-week University of Florida program offering advanced research experiences in biomedical science and environmental science and toxicology. Biomedical participants explore techniques such as DNA science, protein science, CRISPR, and gel electrophoresis, while environmental students investigate topics including pollution, aquatic health, epidemiology, invasive species, and conservation.

name: Florida Youth Institute (FYI)
title: Agricultural and Life Sciences Research Program
department: College of Agricultural and Life Sciences
applicationWindow: The 2026 Florida Youth Institute offered two sessions, June 28-July 3 and July 5-10, for rising 11th- and 12th-grade students. U.S. students may apply, although availability for students outside Florida is limited. Students should check the official program page for the next application cycle.
ratingNote: A useful agriculture and life-sciences research exposure program that gives students experience investigating real food-security and natural-resource challenges, although it is not equivalent to an independent laboratory internship.
summary: The Florida Youth Institute introduces high school students to agriculture, life sciences, biological engineering, food security, and natural resources through the University of Florida College of Agricultural and Life Sciences. Students explore laboratories and research environments, investigate major global agricultural challenges, and develop research-based recommendations that they present to experts.

name: NASA SEES High School Summer Intern Program
title: NASA Earth and Space Science Research Internship
applicationWindow: The 2026 program was open to current high school sophomores and juniors who were U.S. citizens and at least 16 years old by July 5, 2026. The on-site internship ran July 5-18, followed by a research symposium July 20-21, with additional virtual research projects offered during June and July. Students should check the official SEES website for the next application cycle.
ratingNote: An exceptional high school research experience combining UT Austin mentorship with authentic NASA-related research, scientific data analysis, visualization, field investigations, and a final research symposium.
summary: NASA SEES gives high school students the opportunity to work with NASA and aerospace experts on authentic Earth and space science research through UT Austin's Center for Space Research. Projects can involve remote sensing, engineering, scientific data analysis, visualization, and field investigations, with students ultimately presenting their research.

name: Science and Engineering Apprentice Program
title: Applied Research Laboratory R&D Apprenticeship
applicationWindow: The Science and Engineering Apprentice Program is intended for students during the summer between high school and college, with preference given to students planning to attend UT Austin. Participants complete a summer research-and-development project at Applied Research Laboratories and produce a technical report and research presentation. Students should verify current application dates and eligibility requirements.
ratingNote: A highly substantial research experience because participants work in a professional laboratory R&D environment, complete an individual summer project, write a formal technical report, and present their research.
summary: The Science and Engineering Apprentice Program gives graduating high school students experience in the research-and-development environment of UT Austin's Applied Research Laboratories. Apprentices work on summer-long projects involving engineering, computing, physics, mathematics, or related applied research and conclude by producing a technical report and research presentation.

name: High School Research Initiative (HRI)
title: UTeach and Freshman Research Initiative High School Research Program
applicationWindow: Participation occurs through Texas high schools partnering with the High School Research Initiative, with particular emphasis on expanding research access for rural students. Participating classes collaborate with UT Austin Freshman Research Initiative laboratories on research modules lasting approximately one to five weeks.
ratingNote: A legitimate student-driven research experience connected directly to UT Austin research laboratories. Students develop research questions, conduct experiments, analyze data, and communicate their findings, although participation depends on attending a partner school.
summary: The High School Research Initiative connects participating Texas high school classrooms with UT Austin Freshman Research Initiative laboratories. Students engage in authentic research by developing scientific questions, designing experiments, collecting and analyzing data, writing technical reports, and presenting findings to UT mentors or research faculty.

name: Hofmann Lab / Crockett High School Research Internship Program
title: Year-Long High School Laboratory Research Internship
department: Hofmann Laboratory / Department of Integrative Biology
applicationWindow: Participation occurs through the research internship partnership involving Crockett High School and UT Austin laboratories. Students are matched with STEM laboratories based on their research interests and spend two half-days each week during the academic year working toward long-term research projects while receiving school credit.
ratingNote: An unusually substantial high school research experience because students spend an entire academic year embedded in UT Austin STEM laboratories and work toward long-term original research projects under university mentorship.
summary: The Hofmann Lab has documented a year-long High School Research Internship Program with Crockett High School that connects students with UT Austin STEM laboratories. Students are matched according to their scientific interests and spend two half-days each week conducting long-term research while receiving academic credit through their school.

name: Research & Statistics Camp
title: Independent Research and Statistics Summer Program
applicationWindow: The program is designed for students who have completed 8th or 9th grade by the start of the summer session. Participants spend five weeks developing an independent inquiry while studying research methods, statistics, and technical writing. Students should check UTeach Outreach for current application dates and program details.
ratingNote: A valuable research-development opportunity for younger students because participants undertake an independent inquiry while learning statistics, research methodology, and technical writing, although it is not equivalent to a faculty-lab internship.
summary: UT Austin's Research & Statistics Camp gives younger high school students five weeks to develop an independent research inquiry while receiving instruction in research methods, statistics, and technical writing.
